Try it on the accounts still calling: It goes in beside Pepper without a project, so you can start with the handful of accounts that never adopted the storefront and judge it on those before deciding anything bigger.

@graph.name: Three steps, and no migration to schedule
@graph.description: There is nothing to migrate here, and Pepper is left as it is. Send us the guides your office works from, and we do the loading.

step.name: Send over your guides
step.text: Whatever form they are in now. We load each account's items and your prices into one admin screen, matched to your SKUs.

step.name: Your accounts get the app
step.text: We create the account and the kitchen downloads the app. Most are ordering before that day is out.

step.name: It shows up ready
step.text: Confirmed by the customer, with a number and the time it was sent, in the format your system takes.

@graph.name: Do we need a Pepper alternative so kitchens can check their own spoken orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Pepper can stay as it is, Order Agent included, while we add an app where kitchens say what they need and check every item themselves. The ones already ordering on Pepper's storefront carry on there. Nothing has to be switched off to try it.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Pepper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at running the whole business on one platform: storefront, reps, collections and pricing. Pepper is built wide for that, and we are not trying to be. Where we help is narrower: a reorder your account speaks and signs off, and plenty of people looking for a Pepper alternative turn out to want exactly that one thing.

@graph.name: Is there a link between VoiceOrder Solutions and Pepper?

acceptedAnswer.text: None. We have no connection to Pepper and no shared support arrangement. Each product hands its orders to your own system separately, ours by email with a file attached, over EDI or the API, or into QuickBooks. When ours go in by a direct feed, both land in the same system; by email, ours arrive as a file your team opens like any other.

@graph.name: Will our accounts be juggling Pepper's storefront and your app?

acceptedAnswer.text: They should not have to. Kitchens already ordering through the storefront can stay on it. Offer our app to the ones who still call, text or leave a voicemail, because those orders cost your desk the most time. Anyone who keeps calling is handled as now, with no order number from us, since numbers come only with what our app sends.

@graph.name: How quickly can we actually be taking orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors reach that point in a day or two, and most of their customers send a first order the same day. There is no IT project and Pepper runs throughout, which is a very different job from the window Pepper publishes for standing up its whole platform.

We quote by distributor, so tell us about your operation and we will price it. Pepper quotes too and publishes no rate card. Since you would be keeping Pepper, the figure worth asking for is what our app adds on top.

@graph.name: Do our customers need new hardware or a tablet?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Our app runs on the iOS or Android phone already in their pocket. We send nothing out, there is nothing to bolt to a counter, and no device for you to support.

@graph.name: Where do the Pepper details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pepper's own website. The module list, the storefront and Order Agent descriptions and the implementation window were all read off usepepper.com on 10 October 2026, including their own post on how long an implementation takes. We have not repeated their marketing numbers here. If any of it has changed since, this page is the thing that is out of date, not them.
